subject: Re: Starlabs - escrow-style controls for private deployment
messages:
From: Olivia Stone <olivia.stone@starlabs.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@starlabs.com
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Escrow-equivalent for on-prem deployment - Starlabs request

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is asking that we get an "escrow-equivalent" for the private deployment option before we can proceed to signature. Their asks are fairly standard for us: a way to recover service continuity if Redwood were to become unavailable (technical handover or third-party custodian), attestation of the build artifacts and operator access boundary, and a schedule for delivery of evidence (audit logs, operator runbook) post-commit.

I've attached Starlabs_Escrow_Request.pdf which summarizes our legal team's preferred controls. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support something short of full source-code escrow (Starlabs would prefer a lightweight solution)? If so we'll share a first-pass contract note to help legal draft the order form.

Olivia
Olivia Stone
Head of Procurement, Starlabs Inc.
olivia.stone@starlabs.com

Attachment: Starlabs_Escrow_Request.pdf (PDF, 234KB)
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Stone <olivia.stone@starlabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-09T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escrow-equivalent for on-prem deployment - Starlabs request

Hi Olivia — appreciate the clarity and the PDF. Short answer: yes, we can propose an "Escrow-Lite" approach that meets the goals you described without full source escrow. High level proposal below; happy to put formal language into the MSA/order form if this aligns with Starlabs legal.

Proposed Escrow-Lite (summary):
- Custodial handover: Encrypted operator artifacts + runtime container images + boot script bundle uploaded to a neutral object store (signed, time-stamped). Access delegated to a named custodian (e.g., major cloud provider account or appointed law firm) under narrow release triggers (insolvency, multi-month non-responsiveness, proven SLA failure).
- Key management: Customer-held KMS with split-access for operator credentials; Redwood provides sealed operator credential packages that can be unsealed only with a two-party threshold (customer security designee + custodian).
- Evidence schedule: Quarterly attestations (signed) plus one-time handover package within 30 days of trigger; production audit logs and runbook snapshots delivered on a 30/90 cadence for the first year post-release.
- Attestations & verification: Build artifact hashes, SBOM export, and HMAC-signed manifest provided by Redwood. Option for a third-party verification check at customer's expense.

If that maps to Starlabs' risk model, our legal team can produce redline language for an Order Form addendum (deployment-handback exhibit). I'm looping in Karthik (IP & contracts) and Lauren (security/compliance) to draft the initial redline.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm that the release triggers above are acceptable to Starlabs legal (insolvency, sustained SLA breach, or willful data misuse).
2) If yes, our legal will produce Escrow-Lite Exhibit v1 and share for Starlabs review (target next-week turnaround).
3) If you prefer custodian recommendations, we can propose a short list (law firms / custodian services).

Thanks — I want to keep this light and executable so we don't block the deal.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Escrow-equivalent for on-prem deployment - draft redlines attached

Team / Olivia — I drafted an initial redline for the Escrow-Lite Exhibit and attached it as RI_redline_EscrowLite_v1.docx. High level legal points and places Starlabs should watch out for: 

Key legal notes (summary):
- Release triggers: we narrowed triggers to (a) Redwood insolvency/assignment of assets, (b) failure to meet SLA for a consecutive 90-day period after cure rights, and (c) court order. Starlabs' original ask included "non-responsiveness" — that's vague; we should align on measurable thresholds.
- Scope of artifacts: we limit to runtime artifacts, deployment manifests, and reproducible build manifests (hashes/SBOM). We explicitly exclude proprietary model weights and training data. This needs a clear clause.
- Custodian authority: custodian acts only as an escrow-enforcement agent; any release requires dual authorization (customer consent OR court order + Redwood counterparty notification). We should avoid a unilateral release path.
- Liability & indemnity: propose a capped liability specifically for release events; unlimited indemnity clauses from either side won't fly.

I've annotated specific sections where Starlabs may request broader scope. Olivia — when your legal reviews, please flag the exact release triggers you need and any custodian preferences.

Attachments: RI_redline_EscrowLite_v1.docx (Word doc, tracked changes)

-karthik

Looping in ops/eng next steps — quick operational checklist so the legal redline maps to what we can deliver without long project timelines: 

Operational feasibility checklist (for internal use):
- Artifact snapshot process: define exact image names, manifest format, and SBOM exporter. (Owner: @infra-release)
- Custodian upload flow: automated upload to presigned neutral bucket + HMAC-signed manifest generation. (Owner: @infra-release)
- KMS split-access integration: confirm we support customer KMS import and sealed packages. (Owner: Security Eng)
- Evidence cadence: automation for quarterly attestations + ad hoc evidence pull on approved triggers. (Owner: Compliance)

I can kick off owners and estimate work if legal indicates final scope. Camila — if Starlabs is OK with our Escrow-Lite summary, I'll carve out engineering time for the artifact automation and provide an ETA (I think 3-5 weeks for a minimal pipeline).

-Jasmine
